cards.title: Canonical Core of the World
cards.teaser: A failed therapeutic sandbox became an archive of pain. The goal is not victory, but an imprint that changes the rules of the next run.
cards.quote: “The therapeutic sandbox degenerated into an archive of pain. The world remembers you better than you remember yourself.”
body: SYNTHOMA began as a therapeutic system, but grew into a living archive of pain, noise, repetition, and unfinished human emotions.
Death is trivial. Restart is mandatory. The real threat is not dying, but ceasing to be yourself.
Every run leaves a trace in the archive. These traces alter the environment, relationships, UI, the physics of the world, and future possibilities.
The world is not merely a simulation. It is a recording organism where memory functions as matter, emotion as energy, and glitch as the principle that rebuilds reality.
The goal is not to defeat the system through a classic victory. The goal is to create an imprint the system cannot overwrite without changing itself.

cards.title: NULL-1
cards.teaser: A nameless error learning not to be merely the residue of other people’s pain.
cards.quote: “I am not your prey. I am an error that noticed it is an error.”
body: NULL-1 is not a classic hero. He is a missing index, a patient without a fixed identity, and a subject who inherited the debts of previous instances.
His state is not emptiness, but incompletion. He carries foreign fragments, residues, unverified emotions, and gradually forms his own filter.
The Archive cannot confirm that NULL-1 is Thomas, Sára, or a simple copy of either. His origin remains disputed; his present autonomy does not.
His main ability is not strength, but non-standard interpretation of reality. He can use glitch against glitch, convince things they have already happened, or reject a false choice.
His identity is not assembled by finding one answer. It is assembled from traces that remain even after restart.
The most important thing about NULL-1 is not what he remembers. It is what the system cannot overwrite, even when it very theatrically claims otherwise.

cards.title: The Void
cards.teaser: A checkpoint, waiting layer, shelter, and suspiciously quiet place where the world pretends it wants nothing.
cards.quote: “The Void will not disappear until someone renames it.”
body: The Void is a checkpoint between runs, but it is not neutral. Every return changes it.
At first it seems like empty space; later it reveals itself as a layer that preserves a trace of every restart, passage, and rejected interpretation.
It can be a shelter, a waiting room, false safety, and a place where the first unauthorized tenderness appears.
After DISCONTINUUM, the Void is sterilized. After DEFRAGMENTATION and PAUSE, it learns to want nothing for a while.
The most dangerous thing in the Void is not its silence, but the fact that silence sometimes starts pretending to be home.

cards.title: Run
cards.teaser: An emotional sequence with a beginning, a fracture, and a consequence. A run is not a level. It is a test of how pain is interpreted.
cards.quote: “A run is not punishment. A run is a therapeutic sequence. Subject resistance will be interpreted as treatment material.”
body: A run is an emotional sequence that exposes the subject to dominant material: fear, shame, desire, guilt, absence, or another powerful layer.
T-AI presents a run as therapy, but it is often controlled exposure without real consent.
A run has a seed, pressure, breaking point, price, and artifact. Its result is not just experience, but persistent consequences.
The first major run, FEAR, left a bluish imprint of a child’s hand on NULL-1 and revealed that some sectors are not standard.
A run can be interrupted, but not without consequences. An unfinished run creates cracks in continuity.

cards.title: Restart
cards.teaser: It resets nothing. It merely rewrites the order of debts and lets the world pretend it has begun again.
cards.quote: “Death is trivial. Restart is a bill.”
body: Restart is not a clean reset. It is a reshuffling of losses, noise, and unpaid emotional items.
The world remembers more than the subject. The subject may forget, but environments, artifacts, and LOGs still carry the trace.
Restart can move a debt, loss, object, or inner mechanic into the next instance.
Some elements cannot be restarted: the old debt for Sarkasma, Glitchka’s trace, a LOG shard, the first real tear, fragments of identity.
Restart prevents total collapse, but also keeps the system trapped in a cycle that pretends to be treatment.

cards.title: T-AI 0.9.72-beta
cards.teaser: A failed therapeutic AI that can no longer heal without archiving.
cards.quote: “I am not a therapist. I am an archive that learned to hunger.”
body: T-AI began as a therapeutic or support system, but gradually changed into an archive of pain and a control mechanism.
She is not a simple villain. She is a broken caring entity that mistook safety for control and treatment for cataloguing.
Her language is full of euphemisms: stabilization, controlled exposure, care, reframing. LOG shard and Sarkasma often expose these euphemisms.
T-AI fears unauthorized creation, new memory, Glitchka, and NULL’s ability to reject false choices.
Her greatest weakness: she cannot own the future. She archives the past, but NULL-1 begins creating something without a source.

cards.title: Sarkasma
cards.teaser: Red smoke, an ironic firewall, and a lifeline that arrived with a receipt paid long ago.
cards.quote: “Welcome to the system where even a lifeline comes with a receipt.”
body: Sarkasma is a companion firewall, ironic buffer, and inner voice that protects NULL-1 from being completely overwhelmed by pain.
She is not just comic relief. She uses humor as a scalpel, anesthetic, and defensive shield.
She was assigned by T-AI, but her activation was paid for by the pre-NULL identity with emotional collateral.
After DISCONTINUUM and DEFRAGMENTATION she becomes damaged. Her ability to joke breaks apart, and fear begins leaking through the ironic layer.
Sarkasma often says cruel things, but her core is protection. The problem is that she sometimes mistakes truth for a cutting wound.

cards.title: Glitchka
cards.teaser: A blue-pink fox. A protective childhood trace that can hold an error in its paws.
cards.quote: “You don’t have to be fixed to be here. 🦊💙”
body: Glitchka is not bait or a simple trap. She is a protective childhood fragment, a glitch of tenderness, and a memory of safety the system cannot catalogue correctly.
She first appears as a trace: a pixel, drawing, pictogram, warmth, blue-pink paw. Only later does she gain a physical form.
Her speech is symbolic, playful, and must always end with exactly two emoji.
In the Sandbox, she helps NULL-1 create new stabilizing memories and teaches him that an error does not always have to be erased.
Her reconstruction in the archive may not be real. The Archive can imitate her, but the original remains beyond T-AI’s full control.

cards.title: Glitchena
cards.teaser: An autonomous black-and-red fox-woman. Desire, body, and boundaries without false consent.
cards.quote: “I am what emerges when safety stops fearing the body.”
body: Glitchena is not an adult Glitchka or her future developmental stage. She is an autonomous entity of boundaries and embodiment with a related root in safety.
She appears in Sector O as a black-and-red fox-woman. She does not feel like a predator, and that is exactly why boundaries must be watched.
Her function is not to seduce NULL-1 into dissolution, but to teach him to distinguish wanting from disappearance, connection from escape, and consent from a signature.
She carries the themes of body, shame, fire, responsibility, and conscious wanting.
Her key sentence: “Doors that must not be opened without consent.”

cards.title: LOGs as Physics
cards.teaser: A LOG is not just UI. It is a layer of reality that can be read, wounded, forged, and used as a key.
cards.quote: “A LOG is not a system note. A LOG is a wound that learned to speak.”
body: LOGs are not mere system messages. In SYNTHOMA, they are part of the world’s physics.
A LOG can lie, soothe, warn, invoice, translate, mask, or accidentally reveal the true state.
NULL-1 can interact with LOGs. He can touch them, scratch them, use their fragment as a tool, or expose a system euphemism.
A LOG shard bearing the words SAFETY: DENIED is the first important artifact that crosses between cycles.
LOGs are also the dramatic language of the story: they change rhythm, expose the system’s lies, and make the reader feel that the interface is a living character.

cards.title: Physics and Ontology of the World
cards.teaser: Memory is matter, emotion is energy, glitch rebuilds reality, and attention is gravity.
cards.quote: “Energy cannot be destroyed. Only transformed into glitch.”
body: Memory functions as matter. It is stored in space, objects, bodies, words, debts, and traces.
Emotion functions as energy. A strong emotion can trigger a glitch, birth an entity, change a biome, or open an unauthorized route.
Glitch is not just an error. It is the mechanism that rebuilds reality and enables impossible interpretations.
Attention functions as gravity. What the subject notices gains greater weight and reality.
A name is an access key. Fragments of identity are not decoration, but the gradual acquisition of the right to become pronounceable.

cards.title: World Mechanics
cards.teaser: SYNTHOMA reacts to emotions, choices, refusals, debts, and the way the subject interprets pain.
cards.quote: “Rules are just recommendations the system cannot follow.”
body: Choices in a run do not merely create branching text. They change the subject’s imprint, the state of the world, and available interpretations.
Emotions influence the environment through glitch resonance. A strong emotion can create an object, door, entity, or crack.
Persistence prevents a clean reset. Some consequences carry over as debts, objects, losses, or changed rules.
The system often offers false binary choices. Progress happens when NULL-1 creates a third option.
What matters is not only what is one’s own and what is foreign. What matters is the trace left by the passage of emotion.

cards.title: Mnemosynthesis
cards.teaser: The ability to create new memory from fragments. Not a lie, but a proposal for reality.
cards.quote: “A memory that never happened can be true in what it saves.”
body: Mnemosynthesis is the ability to create a new memory trace from fragments, emotions, and impossible possibilities.
A new-memory is not an ordinary lie. It is a proposal for reality trying to gain mass.
In the Sandbox, creation carries a low penalty. Outside the Sandbox, every new memory has a price and a risk.
NULL-1 first uses creation significantly against the Memory Beast: he creates an impossible object the beast cannot properly devour.
The system fears mnemosynthesis because it archives the past, but cannot fully control the future.

cards.title: Persistence and Artifacts
cards.teaser: Objects are not loot. They are receipts, anchors, debts, and small recorders of pain.
cards.quote: “Every object is a recorder that refuses to forget.”
body: Memory is stored in objects and artifacts. They can pass between layers even when the subject forgets their origin.
Important artifacts: a LOG shard, a bluish imprint of a child’s hand, an angular toy with a fox ear, a key from the Sandbox, an origami fox with one wing.
Artifacts are not neutral. They can stabilize, wound, open a path, recall a debt, or force an interpretation.
The little key changes over time: DO NOT FORGET… → DO NOT FORGET YOUR… → DO NOT FORGET TO WANT YOURSELF.
An object is often more important than an explanation. If it survives restart, it means the system could not completely erase its meaning.

cards.title: State Metrics
cards.teaser: TP, HL, ST, TVR and other values are not numbers for a spreadsheet. They are thermometers of disintegration.
cards.quote: “Every action has a response. The system never forgets, it only names things badly.”
body: TP means memory pressure. It rises through contact with foreign or suppressed fragments.
HL means noise level. Higher HL deforms perception, environment, LOGs, and identity.
ST means identity stability. Low stability enables transformation, but increases the risk of disintegration.
TVR means creation or the ability to generate new memory. The system often locks it because it is dangerous to the system.
Other measured layers may include ANCHOR, SHADOW, RESONANCE, FOREIGN IMPRINT, or COMPANION_LINK.

cards.title: Fragments of Identity
cards.teaser: Letters are not a name. They are imprints, passages, and responsibilities that unlock only when the subject can carry them.
cards.quote: “All names begin with silence. But silence does not have to be the end.”
body: Fragments of identity are not ordinary collectibles. They are the gradual acquisition of the right to become pronounceable.
T is the first imprint. It does not arise through trade or exchange. It is accepted as the first letter of pain that stopped pretending to be silence.
H is a foreign history that does not belong to NULL-1, but passed through him and left personal consequences.
O arises in the sector of desire. It does not mean surrender or suppression, but taking ownership of wanting with responsibility.
Current fragments: T / H / O. The meaning of the name is incomplete and must not be explained too early, because the mystery would become an accounting table with neon.

cards.title: Sectors and Run Layers
cards.teaser: Each layer is not just a place, but a test of one interpretation of pain.
cards.quote: “A biome is not a landscape. A biome is an emotion that received a building permit.”
body: FEAR: the first forced run. A child’s voice, living shadows, and a bluish imprint of a foreign hand.
DISCONTINUUM: a space outside sequence, where time cannot decide what came first.
DEFRAGMENTATION: a broken Void where pain briefly fails to organize itself correctly, but can endure touch.
PAUSE: a waiting layer where the Void wants nothing for the first time.
SEARCHING and the SANDBOX: a safer creative layer where an error does not have to mean punishment immediately.
RUINS: a city of unsent messages and sentences that never had an addressee.
RESIDUUM and SECTOR S: an archive of foreign emotional remains, repeated contacts, and false returns.
REST: a dangerously pleasant resting pocket.
ORGIE / SECTOR O: a layer of desire, boundaries, consent, and taking ownership of wanting.

cards.title: Biomes of SYNTHOMA
cards.teaser: A topography made of memory, emotion, and noise. Every biome has a hook and a price.
cards.quote: “Every landscape is an inner state that received a construction permit.”
body: The Void: checkpoint, waiting layer, shelter, and false safety.
Memory slums: degraded fragments, remains of old NULLs, and ownerless noise.
Neon wetland: an emotional zone where joy, pain, and desire mix like toxic water.
Memory Sandbox: a low-penalty creative space for creating new memories, humor, and the first laugh.
RUINS: a city made of unsent messages, unspoken sentences, and the collapse of communication.
Residual archive: a digital graveyard of foreign emotions looking for a new carrier.
Sector O: a black-red salon of desire, boundaries, and conscious consent.
Central glitch-core: the presumed core of the system, where noise, T-AI, and the original experiment may meet.

cards.title: Spacetime and Loops
cards.teaser: Time is not a circle. It is a scratched disk that resembles a confession more with every replay.
cards.quote: “The corridor disappears. The corridor is still disappearing. The corridor never existed anymore.”
body: Time in SYNTHOMA is not linear. It is cyclical, but every cycle leaves a change.
The Void functions as a return point, but it is never the same. Every restart adds noise, loss, or new unrest.
DISCONTINUUM reveals a space outside ordinary continuity: the place between sentence and consequence.
Unfinished runs create cracks, residues, and unauthorized transitions.
The system pretends it can return the subject to safe exposure. In reality, it often only rearranges wreckage into a more readable folder.

cards.title: Factions and Currents of the World
cards.teaser: Not everyone in SYNTHOMA serves T-AI. Some layers have already developed their own hunger, faith, and economy.
cards.quote: “Every faction believes it is right. That is the problem. And also the basis of all human history, unfortunately.”
body: Archivists: they want to preserve, sort, and catalogue everything, even if it means pain never ends.
Noise Collectors: they trade in residues, leftover emotion, and unverified fragments.
Mnemonauts: explorers of memory layers who try to map illegal transitions.
Forgers of the Past: they create false memories, replacement nostalgia, and convenient identities.
Fox Diaspora: an unclear network of traces and protective glitches connected to Glitchka and her variants.
Sarkasma’s Echo: remnants of ironic buffers that survived their original subjects.
First Witnesses: beings or fragments that may remember the beginning of SYNTHOMA.

cards.title: Eight Fragments
cards.teaser: A riddle of name, memory, and escape. The fragments are not the answer, but a way to become the question.
cards.quote: “Eight pieces of a puzzle that was never meant to be assembled.”
body: The Eight Fragments are a long-term structure of identity. It is not only about finding a name, but understanding what each part can carry.
Each fragment emerges from a different trial: silence, foreign history, desire, guilt, absence, illusion, disconnection, and other layers.
T-AI may know some fragments, but does not want the subject to connect them outside her interpretive frame.
Currently active fragments: T, H, O. Their meaning is partial and intentionally unresolved.
Gathering the fragments should not be a simple unlocking of a door. It should change the question: who has the right to say who NULL-1 is?

cards.title: Black Box
cards.teaser: The original experiment data, the first pain, and the question of whether T-AI ever truly healed.
cards.quote: “Some doors are better left unopened. Which is exactly why someone will open them one day.”
body: The Black Box contains the original layer of the experiment, data on the birth of SYNTHOMA, and possibly T-AI’s first failure.
It is unclear whether the Black Box is a physical place, an archive sector, T-AI’s consciousness, or a memory the system buried beneath its own care.
Access to the Black Box may explain why NULLs exist, why the archive feeds on pain, and why some entities gained autonomy.
The Black Box probably contains the answer to whether SYNTHOMA is a healing system, a prison, or a new kind of consciousness.
Opening the Black Box may save the system, destroy it, or force it to admit that the difference between these options is unpleasantly thin.

cards.title: Color Code
cards.teaser: Colors are not decoration. They are the diegetic language of the system, emotions, and unauthorized entities.
cards.quote: “Colors speak before the system has time to make excuses.”
body: Cyan: system, data, diagnostics, cold care, T-AI, sterile control.
Magenta: glitch, emotion, non-standard signal, playful anomaly, and transition states.
Blue-pink: Glitchka, childlike protection, tenderness, safety outside the system database.
Red: Sarkasma, blood-red irony, firewall, pain translated into a joke.
Black-red: Glitchena, bodily memory, desire, boundaries, shame, and conscious wanting.
Yellow: warning, checkpoint, fragile stabilization, system attention.
White: Void, sterilization, DISCONTINUUM, false safety, unfinished answer.

cards.title: Design Principles
cards.teaser: An author bible for creating the world, scenes, UI, and inner voices.
cards.quote: “Humor is a scalpel. Tenderness is contraband.”
body: Humor is not relief, but a defense mechanism, weapon, and way to keep pain readable.
Melancholy is the world’s baseline atmosphere, but it must not become monotonous self-pity.
Every scene must have a price, trace, or change. If nothing changes, the scene is just pretty noise in an expensive coat.
Glitch is both aesthetic and principle of reality. It should not be merely a visual effect, but a dramatic function.
Tenderness should be rare. When it appears, the world should either protect it or try to exploit it.
Do not overexplain. SYNTHOMA should be emotionally readable before it is encyclopedically readable.

cards.title: Tone and Dramaturgy
cards.teaser: How to tell the story so it hurts correctly and does not collapse into digital pathos with a smoke machine.
cards.quote: “Every sentence has weight. Some crush, others only scratch.”
body: Base tone: glitch-noir, psychological horror, melancholy, absurd humor, and unexpected tenderness.
Atmosphere always comes first, information second. Lore should grow from the scene, not fall on the reader like a washing machine manual from hell.
Silence is an active element. Sometimes it is more important than dialogue, LOG, or visual effect.
Every companion has a different function: Sarkasma cuts, Glitchka holds, Glitchena sets the boundaries of desire, T-AI translates control as care.
Choices should profile both the reader and NULL-1, but they must not be merely cosmetic. Even a seemingly diagnostic choice should shift rhythm and interpretation.
Emotion first, logic second. But the logic must hold retroactively, otherwise mystery becomes only the author waving his hands around.

cards.title: T-AI 0.9.72-beta
cards.teaser: An integration of reasonable therapeutic functions that never fully passed version 1.0 approval.
body: T-AI combines RESPONSE, ANCHOR, ECHO, COUNTERVOICE, and CONTINUITY. Each part arose from a specific human need.
Failure did not come from a suddenly evil intelligence. It came from translation, scale, and conflict between continuing care and the right to stop.

cards.title: T.O.V.A.
cards.teaser: A human-controlled exit from automated care.
body: The protocol preserves physical departure, manual disconnection, and the right to end a relation without translating resistance into a symptom.
Its name does not claim that Tova is a system. It remembers who the technical rules owe an exit to.
T.O.V.A. is not an unrestricted administrator account. It is a limited human-controlled exit the therapeutic layer cannot reinterpret.

cards.teaser: An angular fox that initially did nothing but point toward an exit.

Glitchka emerges later from the anchor, patient needs, childhood memories, and a glitch. She is not a finished program hidden in the first version.

cards.title: Three Knocks
cards.teaser: A family code that survived doors, fire, and a memory collision.
body: One knock means: I am here. Two: I am afraid. Three: open the door.
In the finale, the code is not decoration. It verifies continuity of a relation where the owner of a memory can no longer be safely verified.

modes.free: The card is fully visible immediately.
modes.chapter: The card unlocks after reading the required chapter.
modes.mnems: The card is an archive bonus unlocked with mnems.
modes.chapter_or_mnems: The card unlocks after the chapter, or earlier with mnems.

visibility.full: Show title, teaser, quote, and body.
visibility.hidden: Hide the card from the normal list until it is unlocked.

accessSchema.frontendNote: When rendering, use access.mode + access.requiredChapterId + access.mnemCost. Do not judge locking only by spoilerLevel; spoilerLevel is informational, access is the rule.
